note: Verified against legislation.vic.gov.au on 2026-08-14. The Supreme Court (General Civil Procedure) Rules 2015 were replaced by the Supreme Court (General Civil Procedure) Rules 2025 (S.R. No. 85/2025) from 8 September 2025; citations refer to the 2025 instrument. Rule 3.01 rollover turns on days the Court office is closed; the script approximates office-closed days with the weekend-and-public-holiday table, and every computed date carries a warning to confirm the office was open. The appearance rule stays pending-verification because the operative time is the time stated in the writ itself.

computation_provisions.summary: A period reckoned from a particular day excludes that day (s 44(1)) and a period ending on a particular day includes it (s 44(2)); where the time for doing an act expires on a holiday it extends to the next day that is not a holiday (s 44(3)); holiday means a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday appointed under the Public Holidays Act 1993 for the place where the act is to be done (s 44(4)).

computation_provisions.citation: Supreme Court (General Civil Procedure) Rules 2025 (Vic) r 3.01
computation_provisions.summary: Calculating time: any period fixed by the Rules, a judgment or order, or a document in a proceeding excludes the day or event day from which time runs (r 3.01(2)) and includes the end day (r 3.01(3)); for periods of 5 days or less, days the Court office is closed are excluded (r 3.01(4)); where the last day falls on a day the office is closed, the act may be done on the next day the office is open (r 3.01(5)).

evidence.method: Firecrawl scrape of the official authorised in-force version; instrument corrected from the revoked 2015 Rules.
evidence.version: S.R. No. 85/2025, Authorised Version No. 003, as at 1 January 2026

period_rules.label: Appearance after service of writ (service in Victoria; minimum period)
period_rules.citation: Supreme Court (General Civil Procedure) Rules 2025 (Vic) r 8.04(a)(i)
period_rules.trigger: Service of the writ in Victoria
warnings: The operative time for a specific defendant is the time stated in the writ; r 8.04 fixes only the minimum (not less than 10 days for service in Victoria; 21 days elsewhere in Australia; 42 days out of Australia; 30 working days for New Zealand under the Trans-Tasman Proceedings Act 2010 (Cth)). Take the date from the writ itself.

evidence.note: Verified on 2026-08-14 against S.R. No. 85/2025 (r 8.04(a) as substituted by S.R. No. 127/2025) that the rule fixes minimum periods stated in the writ, not an operative deadline the script can compute from service alone; the entry stays pending and fails closed by design.

period_rules.label: Defence where the writ's indorsement of claim stands as the statement of claim
period_rules.citation: Supreme Court (General Civil Procedure) Rules 2025 (Vic) r 14.04(a)
warnings: This limb applies only where the indorsement of claim constitutes the statement of claim; where a separate statement of claim is served, the 30 days runs from service of the statement of claim (r 14.04(b)), and the Court may fix another time (r 14.04(c)).
Rollover is computed as the next weekday that is not a Victorian public holiday; r 3.01(5) turns on days the Court office is closed — confirm the office was open on the candidate date.
